about: Reference ranges for the greatest length of complete bones, used by models/length_check.py to re-rank identifications when the user measures the bone. Keys are 'human' or one of the model's mammal family groups (config.MAMMAL_FAMILIES), then BONE_TYPES names; each entry says which animals it was measured on. A taxon/bone pair that is missing is simply not checked. Birds span sparrows to ostriches, so they get only an upper bound ('upper_bound_only'): the femur and tibia (tibiotarsus) of the ostrich, the largest living bird. That rules a bird out for longer bones and says nothing about shorter ones. Bird wing bones are not covered.

measurement.long_bones: Greatest length, end to end, of a complete femur, humerus, tibia, radius or ulna.
measurement.cranium: Greatest cranial length, glabella to opisthocranion (front of the brow ridge to the back of the skull).

confidence_levels.high: Measured specimen ranges agree with published population statistics.
confidence_levels.medium: Measured specimen ranges from one reference collection; the true range may be somewhat wider.
confidence_levels.low: Covers only part of what the class name includes (e.g. one wild species of a group with larger domestic forms).

sources.osteoid: OsteoID Bone Identification, 'Max Length' on each species/bone page, https://boneidentification.com/bones/<species>-<bone>/ (accessed 2026-09-14). Ranges appear to include juvenile specimens.
sources.human_literature: Adult population statistics used to check the human ranges: femur 39.2-49.0 cm (males) and 36.0-46.9 cm (females) in 200 Indian adults, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8811676/ ; Southern Brazil means femur 46.4, humerus 33.5, radius 26.2, ulna 27.9, tibia 38.8 cm, https://www.bjfs.org/forensicjournal/download.php?arquivo=389 ; Spanish cadaver means, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24611570/ ; female humerus 27.7 +/- 1.1 cm, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7003718/ . Accessed 2026-09-14.
sources.craniometric_literature: Greatest cranial length (g-op) averages about 18-19.5 cm in adult males and slightly less in females, with population means as low as about 16.2 cm reported; standard deviations about 0.6-1.0 cm. Accessed 2026-09-14.
sources.ostrich_morphometrics: Kassem, Tahon, Khalil & El-Ayat 2023, "Morphometric studies on the appendicular bony skeleton of the ostriches (Struthio camelus)", BMC Veterinary Research, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10401756/ : 12 adult males, femur 30.00 +/- 0.23 cm, tibiotarsus 52.00 +/- 0.50 cm. Accessed 2026-10-01.

tibia.note: OsteoID's minimum of 15.9 cm is a juvenile or outlier; the minimum here is about 2.5 SD below adult female means.

cranium.note: Adult; population means minus/plus about 2 SD.
